source: Edward Tuite Dalton, Descriptive Ethnology of Bengal (Calcutta: Government Printing, 1872), comparative table compiled by Babu Rakhal Das Haldar
scope: Complete Juanga target material in Haldar comparative table printed pp. 235–241 (PDF pp. 250–256) and separate Juang vocabulary printed pp. 241–242 (PDF pp. 256–257). The eight adjacent comparison-language columns are controls and not installed.
alternate_rows: Brother (row 17) and dog (row 38) each have two printed alternatives, retained with separate variant-qualified keys.
controls: The eight other printed language columns are Mundari, Santal, Korwa, Kharia, Ho, Kuri/Muasi, Talain/Mon, and Khasi. All 42 × 8 = 336 comparison-control cells are accounted for as 302 present and 34 blank in the inventory mask, and a bounded verbatim sample is in control-sample.json. No control column form is installed or treated as a graph edge.
rights: The exact 1872 source scan is identified as public domain on Wikimedia Commons; Dalton died in 1880 and Haldar in 1887. The PDF and page images are local review cache, not installed assets. Output contains only attributed lexical facts with row/page locators, not source prose or images.
provenance: The printed heading on p. 235 says the comparison tables were compiled for Dalton's Ethnology of Bengal by Babu Rakhal Das Haldar, Assistant Commissioner, Chutia Nagpur. It does not claim Haldar personally elicited each Juanga form, identify speakers, or assign a Juanga elicitation locality. The dialect tag is source-qualified with blank coordinates. '(s.)' annotations are preserved literally as source labels; no automatic Sanskrit borrowing or etymology edge is inferred.
dependence: Dalton 1866 Appendix F pp. 266–267 has a shorter Putoons/Juang table with substantial matching or near-matching entries (man juang, ear lutur, moon lerung/lerang, fire lalai/lálai, water dah/dág). It is treated as a probable earlier partial witness of the same list, not installed as an independent citation. Samuells 1856 explicitly collected a different glossary; this p. 236 pilot has zero normalized exact selected-form matches against its 21 forms. The 1872 table is cited as a compilation, not an independent elicitation.
transcription: All 361 Juanga target cells are inventoried. The complete install includes 196 visually reviewed form rows from 189 accepted cells; 19 typed transcription holds and 153 printed blank target cells are retained in audit. Original spelling and accents are preserved; uncertain source question-mark forms are held. Raw Tesseract OCR is a sequencing aid only and does not override the scan.
overlap: Against 2,049 existing Juang source rows (including Samuells 1856), seven of the 31 selected forms have normalized exact matches in later Pinnow/Zoller source rows; their upstream source dependence is not resolved, so no independent elicitation claim or automatic merge is made. None match Samuells exactly.
audit: reviewed_inventory.tsv preserves the 42-row p.236 pilot and eight-control presence mask; comparative-extension.tsv covers 185 target cells on pp.235 and 237–241; separate-list-inventory.tsv covers all 134 printed Juang-list rows on pp.241–242. The generated audit.jsonl has 361 target decisions. Independent comparative review checked all 30 accepted extension cells, corrected p.235 row15, and ended with zero errors; separate-list sample checked 20/20 with zero errors. Original page images and raw OCR are under images/ and ocr/.
inapplicable: The source provides no stable native script, dictionary sense IDs, or source-stated etymology edges. Eight adjacent comparison-language columns are controls; their forms are not imported. Blank Juanga cells remain in the audit. Coordinates remain blank because source compiler attribution does not identify individual elicitation sites.
deferred: User expressly prohibited database builds and remote execution. Full CLDF/database build, compiled graph/reference/identity validation, complete test suite, and browser QA are deferred. All applicable source-stage extraction, audit, metadata, sound-profile, language/dialect, and focused-test gates are expected to pass locally.
source_page_images: images/page-250.png through page-255.png and images/hi-256.png through hi-257.png (rendered original pp.235–242); raw OCR comparison under ocr/page-250.txt through page-257.txt.
